newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell 26 pct of Drohobych oil refinery.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell 26 pct of Drohobych oil refinery.

text.p: Ukraine's State Property Fund plans to sell a 26 percent stake in the small Drohobych oil refinery to a foreign or domestic strategic investor in the second half of this year, a refinery official said on Monday.
"The government resolved the final plan on the sale of shares in the refinery last month," said Petro Kmetyk, a deputy manager of the Drohobych refinery in western Ukraine.
The government will keep a 10 percent stake in the refinery, one of Ukraine's oldest, and 30 percent will remain in workers' hands.
Managers already own five percent and the balance would be privatised through privatisation certificates held by Ukrainians and investment funds.
Drohobych refined 979,400 tonnes of oil last year compared to 1.18 million tonnes in 1995, but regularly refined more than three million tonnes in the early 1990s.
An investor would be required to upgrade the refinery.
Most of Drohobych's oil is imported from Russia, and some of its final products of gas, diesel and mazut are exported to Slovakia, the Czech republic and Hungary.

Yuri Yekhanurov, who left his job as chairman of the State Property Fund to become economy minister in February, said at the annual European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) meeting in London at the weekend that Ukraine welcomed investor interest from Russian companies.
Ukraine's six refineries have a total annual refining capacity of up to 60 million tonnes (1.2 million bpd) and privatisation has started on each of them.
